items.excerpt: Figma measured what happens when agents get production component context through Code Connect in the Figma MCP server: fewer tokens burned and materially better generated code. A concrete argument for wiring design systems into the agent pipeline rather than letting agents guess.
How Figma changed the way it handles code and design-engineering handoff in order to ship nested folders — a look inside the craft process of a team building with AI-assisted tooling.
Vercel shipped a new v0 API, exposing its prompt-to-UI generation model programmatically so teams can build design-to-code generation into their own tools and pipelines.
Skill packs are now available on skills.sh — bundled, installable agent skills that teams can drop into coding agents, including UI and design-system oriented packs.
An argument that the chat box is a lazy default for AI products, and that designers need interface patterns that expose model capability instead of hiding it behind a text field.
Reading Star Trek's computer as an interaction-design brief: what science fiction anticipated correctly about conversational and ambient AI interfaces, and what today's products still get wrong.
On encoding a designer's taste and decision criteria into durable artifacts so that agents and teammates can reuse it — turning individual judgment into a reusable design asset.

Osmo Studio announced general availability of an AI video pipeline aimed at brand and marketing films, positioning itself as a "storytelling studio with a software factory" rather than a raw generation tool.
LinkedIn added a control that lets users flag posts as "AI slop," a new UI affordance that signals a coming platform-wide design pattern for labelling machine-generated content.
Augmental's MouthPad turns the tongue into a non-invasive human-computer input surface — an accessibility-first interaction-design bet against implantable brain-computer interfaces.
Meta launched Muse Code, its own coding agent, expanding the field of agents that turn prompts and specs into shippable interfaces alongside Claude Code, Cursor and v0.
YouTube spelled out how its monetisation rules treat AI-generated content, drawing a line between augmented creative work and mass-produced synthetic uploads that lose revenue eligibility.
World Creator developer BiteTheBytes previewed Material Creator, a node-based material authoring tool for games and VFX pitched as a real alternative to Adobe's Substance 3D Designer.
Volinga Plugin Pro brings relightable 4D Gaussian Splatting into Unreal Engine, described as a major leap for neural-capture workflows in production virtual art departments.

The Honor 600 packs AI Image-to-Video 2.0 and an on-device dolly-zoom mode, letting one person shoot a Vertigo effect and animate stills without a crew — generative capture arriving in the phone itself.
Klang's SEED runs thousands of AI-controlled characters on a custom inference pipeline so its society keeps living after players log off — a design problem of authoring systems, not scenes.

A practitioner walks through the versioning nightmare of AI-generated character art — variants across models, prompts and revisions — and proposes a matrix system for keeping creative iterations traceable.
A workflow for decomposing a flat generated image back into editable layers, closing the gap between one-shot AI output and an actual production-ready design file.
An agentic-UX pattern argument: never put a one-click Approve button in front of a user without first surfacing the agent's evidence, diffs and reasoning trail.
Artec's Point II laser scanner captures 5.8 million points a second, feeding the high-density scan data that AI mesh-to-CAD and reverse-engineering pipelines now depend on.
Apple is reportedly building its smart-glasses experience design around fitness — a bet that decides what the first mainstream heads-up interface actually looks like.
URXR One mixed-reality glasses passed $500K on Kickstarter in 24 hours, pitched as a wearable monitor — evidence of demand for spatial workspace UI beyond gaming headsets.
Figma's Motion basics series continues with motion paths, teaching designers to author production animation inside Figma rather than handing motion specs to engineers.
Jesse Showalter and Alex Aperios on what actually breaks a creative agency in 2026 — and why the hardest part is no longer the design work itself.
